The petitioner has filed the present petition, inter alia, praying as under:
"Under the circumstances explained above, it is humbly prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus or any other writ or direction or orders to the respondents by directing the respondents to pay just compensation to the petitioner's land bearing Khasra No. for the land bearing Khasra No. 560/424 (4-16), 409 min (11-0), 461(64-12), 450 (3-12) and 451 (4-16) qua his share as per revenue records situated in the revenue estate of Village Jasola, New Delhi, acquired vide Award No.21/92-93, Vill. Jasola along with statutory interest as per Section 34 of the Act, 1894.
It is further humbly prayed that the Respondent No.2/LAC may also please be directed to forward the reference petition filed U/S. 18 of the Act to the Court for adjudication."

sentences.text: The petitioner claims that he is the co-owner of the land comprising in Khasra No.560/424 (4-16), 409 min (11-0), 461(64-12), 450 (3-12) and 451 (4-16) situated in the revenue estate of village Jasola, New Delhi (Subject Land).
Notifications under Sections 4,16 and 17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (LA Act) were published on 22.06.1990 and the land was acquired for the purpose of channelization of Yamuna River.
3. An award being Award No.21/92-93 was pronounced on 18.06.1992.
However, it is the petitioner's case that the possession of the subject land was not taken over immediately after declaration of the said award but was taken over on 19.01.2006.
4. The petitioner states that although the possession of the land was taken over, the compensation was not paid.
5. The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (2013 Act) came into force on 01.01.2014.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (2013 Act)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner states that finding it more beneficial, the petitioner filed a petition [being W.P.(C) No.3819/2015] captioned Jagan Singh v. Union of India claiming that acquisition had lapsed by virtue of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.

entities.text: Jagan Singh v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. The petitioner states that the said petition was disposed of by an order dated 11.08.2013.

This court held that although the acquisition would have to be declared as having lapsed but since the petitioner had stated that he would be satisfied on compensation being paid under the 2013 Act, the same was a reasonable approach.
Accordingly, the court directed that compensation for acquisition of the subject land be paid to the petitioner under the 2013 Act within the period of six months.

The appellant shall make online payment of the amount of costs by transferring the same to the account of the first respondent;
e.

If the compensation determined as per the Award made under Section 11 of the 1894 Act has not been yet paid till date, the appellant and /or the second respondent shall pay the same to the first respondent in the manner provided in clause (d) as above within a period of one month from today.

8. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that in compliance of the directions contained in the judgment dated 13.07.2023 of the Supreme Court, the petitioner has furnished the details of his bank account along with a cancelled cheque to the advocate for the DDA but the compensation has not been received.
9. There is no ambiguity in the directions issued by the Supreme Court This is a digitally signed order.

10. The present petition is, accordingly, disposed of.
